about: Where the Moon is from Earth's centre: ELP/MPP02 fitted to DE405, cut to 4862 of its 35901 terms.

to_j2000.note: Laskar's precession of the ecliptic, as ELP/MPP02 gives it (Chapront and Francou 2003, section 6), from the mean ecliptic of date to the J2000 ecliptic

accuracy: Near the present, a few metres to tens of metres in distance and a few milliarcseconds in direction for the full series (unverified, from memory: Chapront and Francou 2003). The cut: L t^0: 1386 of 12337 kept, dropped at most 1.2 arcsec (typically 0.022); L t^1: 592 of 1199 kept, dropped at most 0.34 arcsec (typically 0.015); L t^2: 210 of 219 kept, dropped at most 0.0085 arcsec (typically 0.0028); L t^3: 2 of 2 kept, dropped at most 0 arcsec (typically 0); B t^0: 785 of 7380 kept, dropped at most 0.66 arcsec (typically 0.015); B t^1: 235 of 516 kept, dropped at most 0.14 arcsec (typically 0.0093); B t^2: 46 of 52 kept, dropped at most 0.0052 arcsec (typically 0.0022); R t^0: 1066 of 12819 kept, dropped at most 0.95 km (typically 0.019); R t^1: 424 of 1165 kept, dropped at most 0.3 km (typically 0.013); R t^2: 114 of 210 kept, dropped at most 0.065 km (typically 0.0068); R t^3: 2 of 2 kept, dropped at most 0 km (typically 0).

sources.text: Chapront, J. and Francou, G. 2003, A&A 404, 735: The lunar theory ELP revisited. Introduction of new planetary perturbations (ELP/MPP02)
